name: Jina Mahsa Amini
story: Jina was a young Kurdish woman from Saqqez who hoped to pursue medical studies. She died in Tehran after being detained by the morality police. Her death became the catalyst for the Woman, Life, Freedom protests.
credit: Portrait: IranWire via Reuters / ABC News. Original image is linked in the source article.

name: Nika Shakarami
story: Nika loved drawing and worked in a Tehran café. Those close to her remembered her independence and artistic talent. She disappeared during the September protests and was later found dead. Her family disputed the authorities’ account; the Omid Memorial documents the differing accounts.
credit: Portrait supplied by the project owner. Original photographer and publication rights are not yet documented.

name: Sarina Esmailzadeh
story: Sarina was a student, poet, and video creator who shared her hopes and everyday life online. The Omid Memorial reports that she died after being beaten during protests in Karaj. The record also documents the authorities’ conflicting account.
credit: Portrait supplied by the project owner. Original photographer and publication rights are not yet documented.

name: Kian Pirfalak
story: Kian was nine. He loved animals, reading, and imagining a future in space or robotics. He died when his family’s car came under fire in Izeh during the unrest. His family’s account of the shooting differed from the official account.
credit: Portrait supplied by the project owner. Original photographer and publication rights are not yet documented.

name: Hamid Mahdavi
story: Hamid was a firefighter from Mashhad. Iran International reports that he was killed during the January protests and describes accounts of him helping the wounded. The outlet notes that the identity of the rescuer in widely shared footage has not been confirmed with certainty.
credit: Portrait: JavidnamaneVatan, archived by The Iran I Know (item 2269). This is separate from the rescue footage.

sources.title: The Iran I Know · Portrait record

name: Neda Aqa Soltan
story: Neda loved music and travel and had taken classes to become a tour guide. She was shot and killed in Tehran during the protests following the 2009 presidential election. Her memorial record preserves recollections from people who knew her.
credit: Portrait supplied by the project owner. Original photographer and publication rights are not yet documented.

name: Mani Safarpour
story: Mani was 18 and loved football, especially Persepolis. He lived in Tehran’s Salsabil neighborhood and had two sisters. The Abdorrahman Boroumand Center reports that security forces shot and killed him during the protests on 8 January 2026. His family remembered his honesty and kind heart. He was buried near Lahijan, in Gilan.
credit: Portrait supplied by the project owner. Original photographer and publication rights are not yet documented.

name: Khodanoor Lajei
tags: Khodanour Khodanur Lojei Lajaei Baloch Baluch
story: Khodanoor was a 27-year-old Baloch man from Shirabad, Zahedan. According to relatives’ accounts reviewed by Factnameh, he was wounded by gunfire in the unrest after Bloody Friday and died in hospital on 2 October 2022. Factnameh examines the conflicting official account and the evidence against it. A widely shared photograph of him bound to a pole came from an earlier detention, not the day he died.
credit: Portrait supplied by the project owner. Original photographer and publication rights are not yet documented.

sources.title: Factnameh · Accounts of Khodanoor’s life, detention and death

name: Hadis Najafi
story: Hadis shared moments of her life on TikTok and Instagram. Before joining the protests, she spoke of hoping that her future self would be glad she had taken part. A United Nations communication reports that security forces shot her while she was peacefully demonstrating in Karaj on 21 September 2022. Her family disputed the authorities’ account of her death.
credit: Portrait supplied by the project owner. Original photographer and publication rights are not yet documented.
